eventMetadata.context_description: **Clear skies, stable high pressure, and light southwesterly winds are driving strong daytime heating across Madrid today, with AEMET issuing a yellow alert for maximum temperatures.** Official forecasts peg the daily high at 37°C, while multiple numerical models and real-time observations show afternoon readings climbing toward 36–38°C under minimal cloud cover and low humidity. These conditions align with the market-implied odds favoring 38°C (69%) and 37°C (23%), as traders weigh the potential for the official Retiro or airport station to record a peak at or above the AEMET point forecast. Historical September baselines and current model consensus support limited upside beyond 39°C, keeping higher outcomes at single-digit probabilities. Updated AEMET observations and any late-afternoon model adjustments remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent cloud cover, widespread showers, and high humidity are capping daytime heating in Taipei, with official forecasts and model consensus pointing to a maximum near 30–31°C on September 4 amid light winds and frequent precipitation. Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration and multiple global models show daytime peaks in the 27–32°C range, consistent with the market’s tight clustering around 30–32°C; the 31°C outcome leads because showers often interrupt peak insolation without fully suppressing warmth. Historical September averages near 29–30°C provide context, yet short-term variability in rainfall timing and cloud thickness introduces the main uncertainty for the exact high. Updated model runs and Central Weather Administration briefings tomorrow morning will refine the precise maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Malaysian Meteorological Department forecasts for September 4 project a maximum of 35°C under hazy conditions with isolated afternoon thunderstorms, consistent with early September climatology where daily highs average near 32°C but can peak higher amid variable moisture. Model outputs diverge modestly due to uncertainty in cloud cover, timing of showers, and steering winds, with several global and regional runs indicating afternoon peaks closer to 33–34°C. Recent surface observations near 32–33°C and persistent haze from regional sources support the market's strong weighting toward 33–34°C as the most probable outcomes, while the low 7.5% implied probability on 35°C reflects expectations that convective activity or thicker cloud decks will cap the daily high. Updated METMalaysia briefings and next model cycles remain key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Strong south-easterly winds and clearing skies after Wednesday-Thursday showers are positioning 19–20°C as the most probable maximum temperatures for Cape Town on September 4.** 

Multiple forecast models, including those from WeatherBug, Globalmeteo, and Yr.no, indicate a high near 19–20°C (roughly 66–68°F) under mostly clear to sunny conditions, with peak readings expected in the early-to-mid afternoon before winds strengthen further. These conditions align with typical early-spring patterns in the Western Cape, where September daytime maxima average around 18–20°C, though the persistent SE flow—flagged in South African Weather Service advisories for damaging gusts—often prevents stronger warming by enhancing mixing and evaporative cooling. 

Trader consensus, reflected in the 48% implied probability for exactly 20°C and combined ~41.5% for 19°C or 21°C, tracks this narrow forecast range closely, with lower probabilities assigned to outliers that would require either unexpected cloud cover or a sharper wind shift. Updated model runs overnight or early on September 4 could still nudge the exact peak by 1°C, but current observational trends and pressure gradients support the market’s tight clustering around 19–20°C.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the William P. Hobby Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 4 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=khou

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and model guidance for Houston on September 4 points to a high near 91°F under partly sunny skies with a 40-50% chance of afternoon thunderstorms amid high humidity and light easterly winds. This consensus, aligned with the early-September climatological average of roughly 91°F, underpins the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 88–93°F. Key differentiating factors include the precise timing and coverage of convection, which can suppress peak readings by several degrees if storms initiate before afternoon maximum heating, versus clearer intervals allowing fuller insolation and slightly higher values. Dew points near 75°F and heat indices above 100°F further signal limited evaporative cooling, while any overnight or morning cloud persistence could tilt outcomes toward the lower bins. Updated model runs and local observations will refine these variables ahead of market resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klax

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office and ensemble model guidance indicate a high of 22–23 °C for London on 5 September, driven by a west-to-northwesterly flow under building high pressure that favors mostly clear to partly cloudy skies and light winds. This keeps daytime maxima near or slightly above the early-September climatological average while suppressing significant warm advection or strong insolation. Updated runs over the past 48 hours have shown little shift, with minimal model spread around the central forecast and only modest upside risk if cloud cover decreases further. Trader consensus reflected in the market—43 % on 23 °C and 33 % on 22 °C—aligns closely with this guidance, while the smaller probabilities assigned to 24 °C and 21 °C capture residual uncertainty in timing of any frontal passage or diurnal variation.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent tropical moisture and widespread cloud cover from ongoing monsoon patterns are capping daytime heating in Taipei, keeping forecast highs clustered around 29–32°C for September 5. Recent model runs show variable rainfall timing and intensity—stronger or earlier showers would favor the 31°C outcome by limiting insolation, while clearer intervals could allow brief warming toward 32–33°C. Northwest winds and high dew points near 25°C further moderate peaks, consistent with September climatology where afternoon convection often prevents extremes. Traders appear to weigh these near-term uncertainties evenly across the top three bins, with resolution hinging on the final Central Weather Administration analysis.

Minor differences between 17 °C and 18 °C hinge on exact rainfall timing, boundary-layer mixing, and any brief clearing that could allow an extra degree of warming before peak heating. Updated 00Z and 12Z model runs plus Roshydromet guidance will refine these thresholds ahead of market resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kaus

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Historical September 5 averages near 94°F provide climatological context, while model spread and timing of any convection introduce uncertainty around the exact maximum. This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Chicago O'Hare Intl Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kord

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service forecasts and ensemble guidance point to a moderating air mass arriving via northeast flow over the Great Lakes ahead of September 5, shifting Chicago from the early-month heat dome that produced mid-90s readings. This pattern favors daily maxima near 81–83°F at official stations, with lake-breeze effects and possible morning cloud cover or light showers capping peaks in the lower 80s while limiting extreme warmth. Trader consensus around the 80–83°F outcomes reflects this consensus trajectory, tempered by model spread on exact wind speeds, timing of any weak disturbance, and the difference between inland versus lakeside observations that historically adds 2–4°F variability on transitional days. Updated NWS model runs and local climatology comparisons will refine probabilities through the weekend.
